implement: legion-worker: the phase's mechanics, and its references/pr-body.md (the proof shape and the simplify pass), references/skip-checks-trailer.md (no code push carries the trailer) and references/default-branch-check.md (the commits' App identity before the push).
ce-simplify-code: the change rewrites a shared test helper into three, so the simplify pass runs over the rewritten helper before review.

asd-ste100: the two settings descriptions and the AGENTS.md sentence are parsed by operators and by agents with nobody to resolve ambiguity, and a misread of the WARN/ERROR bound costs an operator an outage call.
envoy: the completion report and any decision go to the architect's role topic, never to agent://.
test: legion-worker: the tester's phase, and references/pr-body.md for the proof entries it must record, each re-run at the head.
envoy: reporting to the architect and asking the implementer through its role topic.
review: legion-worker: the reviewer's phase, with references/review-threads.md (replying to and resolving threads) and references/merge-gate.md (approval of the head by SHA).
ce-simplify-code: the reviewer judges the simplify pass over the rewritten helper.
asd-ste100: the three prose edits are the substance of items 1 and 2, so the review reads them as text an agent or operator must parse without help.

findings.finding: The spec's suggested fix (reconcileFailure matching the ERROR alone) cannot fire inside the helper's wait: the ERROR needs RepairGrace (60 s, internal/bus/nats.go:551) of stall while reconcileWait is 30 s (cmd/dispatch/stream_replicas_test.go:36), whose expiry is a t.Fatalf; settings_test.go:922, which expects a refusal and takes 0.20 s today, would fatal at 30 s.
findings.answer: Decision D1 of the plan: the ordinary start stops on no logged failure at all and fails the test at reconcileWait naming the last one; the refusal caller moves to a helper of its own that returns the first logged failure at once; a repair variant drives the repair. The planner measured both numbers and recorded the departure from the spec's starting point.

findings.finding: bus.WithReconnectErrClock would let the grace pass fast, but startDispatchStream builds its client with main's options alone and its doc comment sells that as 'exactly as main makes it'.
findings.answer: Decision D3: no clock and no extra ConnectOption. D1 needs no grace to pass, so the helper keeps building its client exactly as main does.

findings.finding: 'A final refusal' is undefined, and nothing typed at the helper's seam separates a permanent refusal from a transient one (refusedSettings prefixes the setting onto a timeout too, internal/bus/stream.go:580-594; bus.ErrRefused is publish/KV only).
findings.answer: Decision D1 makes finality the caller's statement rather than a classification: the start helper never stops on a retried failure, and the caller that wants the first refusal calls the refusal helper. No new classifier is exported from internal/bus.

findings.finding: The repair cannot be driven from a timer goroutine: testnats.Server.Start, Server.Stop and Cluster.AwaitReady call t.Fatal* (internal/testnats/nats.go:332-341, 275-278; cluster.go:146-160), which Go forbids off the test goroutine, and the helper blocks that goroutine. The issue's 'Stop/Restart' is also imprecise: Restart rewrites the whole configuration file (nats.go:403-416); Stop plus Start is the pair.
findings.answer: Decision D2: the helper calls the caller's repair func from its own polling loop, which is the test's goroutine, and the plan's Task 1.7 uses Stop plus Start plus AwaitReady.

findings.finding: The new test's wall-clock cost and flake margin are unbudgeted, and cmd/dispatch runs in more than one CI job.
findings.answer: Measured and written into the plan's Risks: the first failure lands 10.0 s in (the JetStream request's own deadline) and the repair 0.8 s later, 12.05 s for the whole test against a 30 s wait; three jobs pay it (ci.yaml:2287, :2570, :2576ff). If -count=5 runs close to 30 s, the implementer raises reconcileWait and says why on the pull request.

findings.finding: Item 1's sentence covers two of at least five stop outcomes: two further 'envoy nats recovery cancelled' sites carry no error (recovery.go:311-313, 363-366), a stop seen before the hooks run logs nothing (75-77), and a stop during the re-subscribe returns through closeStopped with no line (64-68).
findings.answer: Task 2 names the two paths on which a run that failed is reported after a stop, with their guards, and deliberately leaves out the error-less sites, which report a stop seen before an attempt rather than a failed run; the plan says so in writing.

findings.finding: The same 'minute' framing appears in AGENTS.md:2858 and :2900, packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md:224, cmd/listener/main.go:408-412 and infra/aws/rendering/metricfilters.go:113-117, and in an unreleased changelog fragment.
findings.answer: Decision D5: item 2 is the two cmd/dispatch/settings.go descriptions and nothing else. Every other statement already anchors the bound at the connection event or at bus.RepairGrace and is not false; the shipped fragment is a record and is left alone.

findings.finding: 'Names the guard and the log call it describes' means different things for AGENTS.md, which already cites symbols, and for a settings description published to operators through the binary and the docs site, where each row is one markdown cell of about 900 to 1300 characters.
findings.answer: Decision D4: AGENTS.md names each path by symbol; the settings cells state the rule the guard enforces in operator terms, anchored at the connection event rather than at the first retry, and name stall_ms, which both lines carry; the pull request cites reportHookFailure, RepairGrace, hooksDueSince, Client.onReconnect and recoverUntilHealthy by symbol. The planner reported this reading to the architect, which decides if the cell must carry the Go identifiers themselves.

findings.finding: Three of the four acceptance clauses are unmeasurable, and the acceptance command names internal/bus, which items 1 to 3 do not touch.
findings.answer: The plan gives every criterion a surface and a command (the acceptance table), including the before-and-after runs that stand in for the unmeasurable clauses; internal/bus is left unedited and its run is the regression check behind the claims items 1 and 2 make about it (D3).

findings.finding: The issue names no changelog fragment, no docs-site obligation and no settings tests, though the corrected descriptions are published and packages/envoy has a .changie.yaml.
findings.answer: Task 4 adds one Fixed fragment under packages/envoy/.changes/unreleased/ with Issue: pr<number> after the pull request is open, and the acceptance table makes `bun run generate` in docs/site part of the evidence for item 2.

findings.finding: The provenance claim ('each is in a file #2542 touches') was unverified.
findings.answer: Verified by the planner: jj diff -r ab319326 --stat lists packages/envoy/AGENTS.md, packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/settings.go and packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/stream_replicas_test.go.

specDepartures.spec: The spec's starting point for item 3 says reconcileFailure matching the ERROR alone, not the WARN, may be the whole change, and that a refusal that never repairs must still end the start before reconcileWait.
specDepartures.plan: The start helper stops on no logged failure: it waits for the reconcile and fails the test at reconcileWait naming the last logged failure. The one caller that asks for a refusal (settings_test.go:922) moves to a refusal helper that returns the first logged failure as soon as it is logged, so that case ends in about 0.2 s rather than at reconcileWait, and a repair variant runs the test's repair on the test goroutine.
specDepartures.evidence: The ERROR is logged only at stall >= RepairGrace (internal/bus/recovery.go:252-260), RepairGrace is a minute (internal/bus/nats.go:551) measured from the connection event the hooks have not covered (nats.go:560-568, 584-589), and reconcileWait is 30 s with a t.Fatalf at its expiry (cmd/dispatch/stream_replicas_test.go:36, 81-83). An ERROR-only rule therefore never fires inside the wait. Measured by the planner in this workspace: the refusal case passes in 0.20 s today; on a three-member cluster with one member stopped the retried WARN lands 10.0 s in and the repair reconciles the stream 0.8 s after the member returns.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance: each sentence in items 1 and 2 names the guard and the log call it describes.
specDepartures.plan: The AGENTS.md sentence names each path by symbol. The two settings descriptions, which the binary prints and the docs site renders for operators, state the rule the guard enforces (the minute runs from the connection event the hooks have not covered, not from the first retry) and name the stall_ms attribute both log lines carry, without Go identifiers; the pull request cites reportHookFailure, RepairGrace, hooksDueSince, Client.onReconnect and recoverUntilHealthy by symbol.
specDepartures.evidence: The descriptions are published: cmd/dispatch's settings subcommand prints them and docs/site/generators/dispatch-config.ts generates the configuration reference from that output, rendering each row as one markdown table cell; settings_test.go:194-196 requires each Description to be one line. AGENTS.md:2867 by contrast already cites bus.Client.reportHookFailure and bus.RepairGrace.
